extension.summary: A modern, customizable take on Kodi's Estuary.
extension.description: Requires Kodi 22 (Piers) or newer. It will not install on Kodi 21 or earlier.[CR][CR]Estuary 8 brings Kodi's classic Estuary into the present: a clean, modern interface with rich skin settings, smart home widgets, and a light, uncluttered layout that stays fast and familiar for Kodi Piers 22. Yours to shape.
extension.news: [B]0.1.44[/B][CR]- New setting under Skin Settings, General, in the Bottom Bar section: "Always show RSS feed". It is off by default and nothing changes until you turn it on.[CR]- With it on, the RSS ticker stays on screen right across the menus and, for the first time, over playing video, live TV and music. Until now it appeared on the Home screen only, and vanished the moment you moved down onto a widget row.[CR]- Kodi's own RSS switch still decides whether anything draws at all. With Settings, Interface, Skin, "Show RSS news feeds" turned off the strip stays empty, and this button takes you to that setting rather than switching something that cannot act.[CR]- While the ticker is on, the media flags and the bottom-strip counters step aside so it has the strip to itself. Turn it off and they come straight back; the separate "Show media flags" setting is never changed.[CR]- Over playback the ticker sits along the bottom on a soft dark fade so it stays readable over bright video, and it hides itself whenever the player OSD, the info dialog or a seek is on screen. The settings windows keep their description text instead.[CR][B]0.1.43[/B][CR]- The Home Live TV item now opens the TV Guide. It used to open the channel list; one press from Home lands on the guide instead.[CR]- Menu editor: "Change action" can now reach the Live TV destinations. Its TV category lists Channels, Guide, Recordings, Timers, Timer rules and Search, and picking one changes only the action, leaving the item's label, thumbnail and submenu exactly as they were. Before this build that category held only per-channel folders, so the Guide and the other windows could not be picked at all.[CR]- The picker also gains a "Custom action..." row pinned to the top, for typing any action by hand with the current one pre-filled. The blank, unlabelled row that used to sit at the bottom of it is gone.[CR]- Needs script.estuary8.shortcuts 3.0.1.6 or newer, which carries the picker half of this fix. Install that zip first.[CR][B]0.1.42[/B][CR]- The default theme background image is updated.[CR][B]0.1.41[/B][CR]- Streaming search now shows its results in the List view, a plain single-column list, rather than the InfoWall poster wall it opened in before. Nothing else about search changed: the same results are found and filtered exactly as in 0.1.40, only their layout is different.[CR][B]0.1.40[/B][CR]- Choosing a search provider is now configuration only. Under Skin Settings, Search, picking a provider records your choice and leaves you in Skin Settings. It used to start a search the instant you picked one, and on a fresh or wiped profile that meant a keyboard opened in your face while you were only trying to turn streaming search on. Enabling or disabling streaming search and the Search Movies and Search TV Shows switches were already configuration only and stay so. The Home magnifier remains the only control that ever starts a search.[CR]- Streaming search results no longer open with a back arrow as the first item. When a search returns nothing to show, the wall now presents a single "No matching results" card instead of an empty page. Kodi's stock video window inserts a ".." parent item as the only entry whenever a listing is empty, ignoring the show-parent-items setting, so an empty result set used to arrive as a lone back arrow; a non-empty listing avoids it. Verified on a clean Kodi 22 bench by reading the container: item one is the result card, not the parent folder.[CR][B]0.1.39[/B][CR]- Streaming search now ships switched OFF. On a fresh or wiped profile the Home magnifier opens the standard search dialog, with Search local library, Search add-ons, Search YouTube and Search TheMovieDB, instead of running a streaming provider search. Nothing is removed: turn streaming search back on under Skin Settings, Search, and the magnifier returns to the provider search.[CR]- What changed: first-run code on the Home screen used to switch streaming search on the first time Home loaded, so a new install defaulted to it whether you wanted it or not. That seed is gone, so the default is now off and stays off until you set it yourself.[CR]- The streaming result filter (plugin.video.estuary8.search) is still a declared dependency and still installs from the Tony.7.Bones repo alongside the skin, so if you do turn streaming search on its results are filtered for real art exactly as before.[CR]- 0.1.38 was built but never published. It carried the filter dependency below but still defaulted streaming search on, which is the one thing this build corrects. Two different builds must never share a version, because Kodi compares add-ons by id and version and a box would keep the one it already had without saying so, so the number moved to 0.1.39.[CR][B]0.1.38[/B][CR]- Streaming search now filters its results out of the box. The result filter (plugin.video.estuary8.search) is a declared dependency of the skin, so Kodi installs it from the Tony.7.Bones repo alongside Estuary 8, and the poster wall shows only titles that carry real art. Until this build the filter had to be installed by hand, and without it streaming search fell back to unfiltered results.[CR]- 0.1.37 was built but never published. It carried everything in the 0.1.37 note below except this automatic install of the filter add-on. Two different builds must never share a version, because Kodi compares add-ons by id and version and a box would keep the one it already had without saying so, so the number moved to 0.1.38.[CR][B]0.1.37[/B][CR]- Streaming search now returns Movies and TV Shows together in one poster wall, all movies first, then all TV shows. Both are read from the same provider and filtered for real art, so junk cards stay out of both.[CR]- Skin Settings, Search now has two plain switches, Search Movies and Search TV Shows, both on by default. Turn either off to pull only the other. The old Anime, Collections, Keyword and Trakt switches, which did nothing yet, are gone for now.[CR][B]0.1.36[/B][CR]- Streaming search now opens its results in the standard poster wall (InfoWall view), the same view the rest of the skin uses, instead of a bespoke results window.[CR]- Art-less junk results are filtered out by a bundled helper add-on (plugin.video.estuary8.search), so the wall shows only titles that actually carry a poster and the placeholder "Next Page" card is gone.[CR]- POV and the other streaming providers are read exactly as Kodi would navigate them and are never modified. If the helper add-on is not installed, search still works, just unfiltered.[CR][B]0.1.35[/B][CR]- The "Hide 'Categories' widget" switch on the menu editor card now actually hides the row. That is the switch you press, and until this build nothing in the skin was reading what it wrote.[CR]- What was wrong: pressing it saves a setting against that one menu item, and every part of the skin that draws the Categories row ignored it. The switch moved, the setting saved, the row stayed. 0.1.34 fixed a DIFFERENT switch with the same job, the one buried inside "Manage items from 'Movies' widget", which is why 0.1.34 did not fix the one you were pressing.[CR]- Measured on a clean Kodi 22 bench, with Movies set to "Lists": switch on, the Categories row disappears and gives its space back; switch off, it comes back with its three tiles. Same for TV shows, and the two are independent, so hiding one leaves the other alone.[CR]- Both switches now work and both are honoured. Which one you see depends on the widget type: a section still on its built-in widget shows "Manage items from 'X' widget", and a section you have switched to "Lists" or "Vertical panel" shows "Hide 'Categories' widget" on the card itself. That is why the switch looks like it is only on some cards.[CR]- Because each switch belongs to a widget type, setting one and then changing that item's widget type can leave the row hidden with its switch no longer on screen. "Reset Item" on the card clears it.[CR]- Your widget rows are untouched, no menu data is rewritten, and no other setting changed.[CR]- No change to Estuary 8 Shortcuts. 3.0.1.4 is current and this build needs nothing newer.[CR][B]0.1.34[/B][CR]- "Hide Categories" now actually hides the Categories row, and it does it the moment you press it. Before this build it did nothing you could see, on any section.[CR]- Two separate faults, both fixed. The switch was only ever read when the skin was loaded, so pressing it changed a stored value and nothing on screen; you had to restart Kodi to see it. And a section you had switched to the "Lists" or "Vertical panel" widget type draws its Categories row from a different place, which was never wired to the switch at all, so even a restart did not help there.[CR]- Measured on a clean Kodi 22 bench: with Movies set to "Lists", switching Hide Categories on used to leave the row sitting there with all three tiles. It now disappears immediately and gives its space back, and switching it off brings it straight back.[CR]- Each section is still its own switch. Hiding Movies leaves TV shows alone, and hiding either leaves the other ten alone. A menu item you created yourself has no Hide Categories switch and is never affected by anyone else's.[CR]- Your widget rows are untouched. So is the order and content of every Categories strip; this build only changes whether the row is drawn.[CR]- Correcting the 0.1.33 note, which claimed more than it should have. It said your existing setup comes through exactly as you left it and that only a brand new profile sees the new defaults. That is true only of a row you had switched on or off by hand. A row you never touched follows the shipped default, so on Movies and TV shows rows you had simply left alone did go off in 0.1.33. Nothing was deleted: every one of them is still in the menu editor with its own switch.[CR]- No change to Estuary 8 Shortcuts. 3.0.1.4 is current and this build needs nothing newer.[CR][B]0.1.33[/B][CR]- Movies and TV shows now open with three Categories tiles instead of the whole strip. "Videos - Library", then "Lists", then "Files", in that order. Everything below those three starts switched off.[CR]- That is 15 rows off on Movies and 8 on TV shows. Nothing was deleted and nothing was renamed. Every one of them is still in the menu editor with its own switch, so put back whatever you want, in whatever order you want it.[CR]- What you have already set up is kept. Your on and off choices are matched to each row by its internal name, no name changed in this build, and a stored choice still beats the shipped default. So a strip you have customised comes through exactly as you left it. What changes is what a brand new profile gets, and what "Reset Item" puts back, which is now three.[CR]- Measured on a clean Kodi 22 install: Movies draws 3 tiles and TV shows draws 3. In 0.1.32 the same two strips drew 15 and 10.[CR]- Music, Music videos, Live TV, Radio, Add-ons and Videos are not touched by this build. Their strips still hold 12, 13, 6, 6, 6 and 7 rows, in the order they were already in, with nothing switched off.[CR]- "Recently added movies" and "Recently added episodes" have been off since 0.1.29 and stay off. They sit fourth in each strip, so they are below the cut either way.[CR]- Your widget rows are untouched, and so is everything else on Home. Only the Categories strip changed, and no menu data is read, rewritten or migrated by this build.[CR]- No change to Estuary 8 Shortcuts. 3.0.1.4 is current and this build needs nothing newer.[CR][CR][B]0.1.32[/B][CR]- A Categories row with nothing in it now takes up no space at all. Not a hidden heading over a gap that is still reserved: the whole band is gone and the first widget row sits at the top of the screen.[CR]- 0.1.31 tried this and got half of it. It asked whether a section had a submenu attached, not whether that submenu had anything in it, so it did nothing on any section that has one. Ten of the twelve built-in sections have one, so on those the empty band stayed exactly as it was.[CR]- The case you are most likely to have hit: switch every row of a section's Categories strip off from the menu editor. The strip is then empty, but the section still counts as having one, so 0.1.31 drew the empty band anyway. Measured on a clean Kodi 22 install with all seven rows of the Videos strip switched off: the "Media sources" row used to start 270 pixels down a 4K screen and now starts at the top, in the same place Games and Pictures start.[CR]- Same for a section whose Categories rows are all hidden by their own conditions rather than switched off, for instance rows that need an add-on you do not have. 0.1.31's note called that one out as known and not fixed. It is fixed.[CR]- Same for a menu item you added yourself, on both Personal widget types, "Lists" and "Vertical panel".[CR]- How it is done, because the obvious way is a trap: the row now asks a small always-running counter how many tiles it would actually draw, and hides itself when the answer is zero. Asking the row itself does not work. Kodi stops refreshing a list the moment that list is hidden, so a row that hid once could never come back, and a build made that way was measured hiding the Categories row on every section including Movies.[CR]- Sections that do have categories are untouched, and that was measured rather than assumed: Movies still draws 15 tiles, TV shows 10, Add-ons 6 and Videos 7, in the same place on screen to the pixel.[CR]- Not exercised, said plainly rather than left to be discovered: the Music, Music videos, Live TV and Radio strips could not be put on screen on the test machine, which has no music library, no music videos and no TV tuner add-on. They are drawn by the same code as the four above, with nothing different but their number, and their call sites are unchanged by this build.[CR]- Your menus are not touched by this build. No menu data is read, rewritten or migrated, no row was renamed and no internal name changed, so anything you reordered, renamed or switched off stays as you left it.[CR]- No change to Estuary 8 Shortcuts. 3.0.1.4 is current and this build needs nothing newer.[CR][CR][B]0.1.31[/B][CR]- A Home section with no categories assigned no longer opens on a blank band. The Categories row is drawn only when that section actually has categories, and when it does not, the space it used to reserve is gone rather than left empty.[CR]- You are most likely to have seen this on a menu item you added yourself, because a new item starts with no submenu. It also happens on any built-in section whose submenu you emptied from the menu editor.[CR]- What it was: the heading above that row was already hidden when there was nothing to list, but the row itself was not. It kept its full height and pushed everything below it down, so the section looked like it had a rendering fault rather than an empty setting.[CR]- Measured on a clean Kodi 22 install: on a section with no categories the first widget row moves up by the whole of the empty band, and the sections that do have categories are unchanged, with Movies drawing 15 tiles, TV shows 10, Add-ons 6 and Videos 7.[CR]- A second fault was found and fixed in the same pass, because hiding the row exposed it: after visiting a section that has categories, an empty section would draw the "Categories" heading on its own with nothing underneath. The heading was reading a leftover count from the previous section.[CR]- Known and NOT fixed, said plainly rather than left to be discovered: a section that has categories where every one of them is currently hidden by its own condition, such as all of them needing an add-on you do not have, still reserves the band. The skin can tell that a section has categories at all; counting how many are showing right now cannot be done here without stopping the row refreshing altogether, which would blank the categories on every other section.[CR]- Your menus are not touched by this build. No menu data is read, rewritten or migrated, no row was renamed and no internal name changed, so anything you reordered, renamed or switched off stays as you left it.[CR]- No change to Estuary 8 Shortcuts. 3.0.1.4 is current and this build needs nothing newer.[CR][CR][B]0.1.30[/B][CR]- Home > Pictures now draws a "Pictures sources" row, listing the picture sources you have added. It never drew one before.[CR]- Home > Games does the same and now draws a "Games sources" row. Also a first.[CR]- What was wrong: both rows were wired to the wrong one of the skin's two similarly named category layouts. The one they used draws a menu item's submenu, and Pictures and Games deliberately have no submenu, so it had nothing to draw and rendered nothing at all. They already carried the folder path the other layout needs, and now use it. Stock Estuary drew picture sources this way; the rebuild this skin came from swapped the layout name and kept the settings.[CR]- Because those two rows now have content in them, the "your pictures library is currently empty" and "your games library is currently empty" panels no longer appear. Those panels only show while the row above them is empty, and the sources row always holds at least the add-ons entry. Videos already behaved this way.[CR]- While it was still reachable, the button on the Pictures panel was labelled "Event log" and opened the Pictures window. It now reads "Add picture source". Kodi has an add-source string for video, music and programs but not for pictures in that run of numbers, which is how the wrong one got picked.[CR]- Movies Categories strip: "Now in Cinemas" and "Next up in Cinemas" now disappear on a box that does not have script.embuary.info installed. Both rows already carried that condition and it was being thrown away, so they drew everywhere and led nowhere on most boxes.[CR]- So on a box without that add-on the Movies strip now draws 15 tiles, not the 17 the 0.1.29 note quoted. Install script.embuary.info and it is 17 again. Both numbers are correct; nothing was deleted.[CR]- That was not a one-row bug. EVERY submenu row's own visibility condition was being discarded, on every home section, because the template that draws those rows only ever tested which section you were on. Conditions are honoured now, so a row that should hide can hide instead of having to be deleted.[CR]- Housekeeping, no visible change: eight home rows were handing a header caption to a layout that does not read one, and the Music row also an item-spacing value. Both were ignored. Removed.[CR]- Your menus are not touched by this build. No menu data is read, rewritten or migrated, no row was renamed, and no internal name changed, so anything you reordered, renamed or switched off stays as you left it.[CR]- No change to Estuary 8 Shortcuts. 3.0.1.4 is current and this build needs nothing newer.[CR][CR][B]0.1.29[/B][CR]- Movies and TV shows: the Categories strip now leads with the three rows most people actually go to. "Videos - Library" first, then a new "Lists" row, then "Files".[CR]- "Lists" is the new one. It opens your video playlists, which is where Kodi files any playlist or smart playlist you make, so those are reachable from the Movies and TV shows rows on Home instead of only from inside Files.[CR]- The first row still reads "Videos - Library", not "Library". That is Kodi's own wording for it, it is what that row has always said, and only its position changed.[CR]- "Recently added movies" and "Recently added episodes" now start switched off in these two strips, so the fourth tile is "Last watched" on Movies and "Titles" on TV shows. Switch either one back on from the menu editor whenever you want it.[CR]- Nothing else was removed and nothing was renamed. Measured on a clean Kodi 22 install: Movies draws 17 tiles and TV shows draws 10, with those three at the front. If you have seen these strips holding only three tiles, that was a box where the other rows had been switched off by hand, not the shipped default.[CR]- Music, Music videos, Live TV, Radio, Add-ons and Videos are not touched by this build. Their strips still hold 12, 13, 6, 6, 6 and 7 rows, in the order they were already in.[CR]- If you had reordered these strips, or switched rows on or off yourself, that is kept. Your changes are matched to each row by its internal name, and no name changed.[CR]- The word "Lists" is new text carried by the skin rather than borrowed from Kodi. Kodi has nothing that reads it: the nearest are "Playlists", which names the folder rather than the row, and "List", which is the name of a view mode. Borrowing a string because it happens to read right is how this skin once ended up with a row labelled "Arial based".[CR]- No change to Estuary 8 Shortcuts. 3.0.1.4 is current and this build needs nothing newer.[CR][CR][B]0.1.28[/B][CR]- Home: a row whose widget type is "Lists (up to 8 items)" or "Vertical panel (1 item)" gets its Categories row back. That is the strip of tiles that sits above the widget rows and opens the section's own sub-pages.[CR]- Before this build those two widget types drew no Categories row at all, on any box, however the row was configured. Every other Home row was unaffected, which is why it looked like something wrong with one menu item rather than with the skin.[CR]- What it was: the skin has two similarly named category layouts. One draws a menu item's submenu; the other is fed an explicit folder path and is used for Video sources and Video playlists. These two widget types asked for the second one and gave it no path, so it had nothing to draw. It now asks for the first one, the same one the ten built-in Home sections that have categories already use.[CR]- "Vertical panel (1 item)" was worse: it named two layouts that do not exist in this skin at all, so there was nothing for Kodi to draw and it said so in the log. Both now point at the real one.[CR]- Only the Categories row changed. Your widget rows, their order, their titles and what they list are untouched, and no menu data is read, rewritten or migrated by this build.[CR]- Known and NOT fixed, said plainly rather than left to be discovered: under Appearance, a widget slot offers six styles for the eight list slots and seven for the panel slot, and only two of those thirteen exist in this skin. "Posters" and "Squares" work, and "Posters" is what a list slot uses unless you change it. The other eleven draw an empty row, and the panel slot's only default, "Posters panel", is one of them, so "Vertical panel (1 item)" now shows its Categories row and still no widget.[CR]- Verified on a Kodi 22 bench: a Movies row set to "Lists (up to 8 items)" drew nothing at all before this change, and after it draws its 17 category tiles above its widget rows. A row set to "Vertical panel (1 item)" went from nothing to its 12 category tiles.[CR][CR][B]0.1.27[/B][CR]- 0.1.26 was built but never published. Everything below was written for it and is unchanged here; only the number moved. A 0.1.26 with different contents sits on a development bench, and two different builds must never share a number, because Kodi compares add-ons by id and version and a box would keep the one it already had without saying so.[CR]- Menu editor: pressing Back leaves the picker. One press, wherever you are in it, and you are back on the item you were editing with nothing changed. It used to go up one step and redraw, and every step of a folder listing opens with the same first row, highlighted the same way, so it read as a dialog you could not get out of. The heading does change as you move through folders; it is the list under it that repeats.[CR]- That covers the pickers our own menu add-on draws. Two routes hand off to Kodi's own file browser instead: "Set thumbnail" then Skin, and "Select background" then Browse for image or folder then Skin. Those still back out one step per press, and no skin can change that.[CR]- The one thing you lose with that: Back no longer steps back up a single folder while you are browsing. Reopen the picker and go in again.[CR]- Add a menu item: the Library list now offers Videos and Music alongside Movies, TV shows and Artists. Those two were there before, buried in a folder called "Use folder names for lookups", which is the name of a scraper setting and meant nothing here.[CR]- Add a menu item: the group of power commands was called "Exit", which is also the name of one of the seven things inside it. It now reads "Power Options", and those seven rows now say what they actually do. Three of them named the wrong action outright: the row reading "Power off system" restarted Kodi, the row reading "Shutdown" rebooted the box, and the row reading "Quit" powered the box off.[CR]- Set thumbnail, and the background pickers: the skin's own folder was listed as "Arial based", which is a font setting. It now says what it holds. In "Set thumbnail" that row reads "Icons"; in both background pickers it reads "Backgrounds". Browsing for a background folder was headed "Profile name"; it now reads "Browse for folder".[CR]- Those rows now carry an icon instead of the bare "+" placeholder they drew before: a folder on the skin's own row, a magnifier on "Browse". Same pair in all three places, "Set thumbnail" and both background pickers. "Browse" is unchanged.[CR]- Menu editor: "Change action" changes the action and nothing else. Your label, your thumbnail and your submenu stay exactly as you left them.[CR]- In 0.1.25 that one button rewrote the whole row. Pressing it on Movies and browsing to a folder renamed the row, swapped the poster thumbnail for a plain folder icon, and deleted all 17 rows of the Movies submenu. Any home row could be hit the same way.[CR]- If that already happened to you, the menu editor now carries a "Reset Item" button. Put the cursor on the row, press it, and the label, the thumbnail, the action and the whole submenu come back. Nothing has to be rebuilt by hand.[CR]- That button is new on screen in this build, not new in the add-on. It was already written and this skin simply never drew it, so a row could be damaged with no way offered to put it back.[CR]- Newly drawn beside it: "Restore Deleted Item", for a row you deleted rather than damaged. "Reset Item" cannot help there, because there is no row left to put the cursor on. This one lists every row missing from the menu, however long ago it went, and puts the chosen one back with its submenu. It returns at the bottom of the menu, so move it up to where you want it. It only appears when there is something to restore.[CR]- "Choose item for menu" still replaces the whole row, which is what that button is for. Use it when you want a row to become a different section; use "Change action" when you only want it to go somewhere else. Its picker does share the Back change above, so backing out of it now leaves the picker instead of stepping up one folder.[CR]- Music videos submenu: the row that opens the music videos library had no label and drew as a blank line. It now reads "Videos - Library", the same as that row in the Movies, TV shows and Videos submenus. It came in with the Piers layout this skin was rebuilt from, and it was asking for a piece of text that does not exist in Kodi 22.[CR]- Housekeeping, no visible change: the Android apps widget declared a widget type that is not a widget type, so the value it saved matched nothing. It showed no symptom and would have started to the moment anything read it.[CR]- Needs script.estuary8.shortcuts 3.0.1.3 or newer, which is where most of this lives. Install that zip first.[CR][CR][B]0.1.25[/B][CR]- Skin Settings: "Show system info on Settings focus" has moved. It was under General; it is now under Home menu, just below "Enable background of 'Power options' shortcut", and it is renamed "Enable system info on 'Settings' shortcut" to match the rows it now sits with. It does the same thing, and whatever you had it set to is kept.[CR]- Skin Settings: the Necessary add-ons page called our menu add-on "Skin Shortcuts". It now reads "Estuary 8 Shortcuts", which is its actual name. The button already installed the right add-on; only the name on screen was wrong.[CR]- Housekeeping, no visible change: a block of unreachable Live TV submenu markup was removed. It could never be shown, and it carried two more rows labelled from an add-on this skin does not install.[CR]- Needs script.estuary8.shortcuts 3.0.1.1 or newer. Install that zip first; it carries a new icon and nothing else.[CR][CR][B]0.1.24[/B][CR]- The Live TV submenu no longer has two blank rows at the top. It had eight entries and the first two were empty and did nothing; it now has the six real ones, starting at Channels.[CR]- Those two rows were labelled from an add-on this skin does not install and never will, so on your box the label came out as nothing at all. They came in with the Piers layout this skin was rebuilt from.[CR]- Radio, Movies, TV shows, Music, Music videos, Add-ons and Videos are untouched, and the Live TV rows that remain keep their own settings. If you had reordered or renamed anything in that submenu, it stays as you left it.[CR][CR][B]0.1.23[/B][CR]- Installing this skin now adds ONE menu add-on, not two. It asked for Estuary 8 Shortcuts and also for the add-on that was forked to make it, so both were installed and both showed up under Program add-ons with almost the same name. Only ours was ever used. The unused one is no longer requested.[CR]- Estuary 8 Shortcuts is now numbered 3.0.1, the version of the add-on it was forked from, so its number says what it is instead of looking like an unrelated, much older add-on. It is the same code that was numbered 1.1.0. Install that zip first; this skin asks for 3.0.1 or newer.[CR]- Sharing that number with the official add-on is safe. Kodi tells add-ons apart by their id, not their name or version, and Estuary 8 Shortcuts has its own id, so neither one can update, replace or outrank the other.[CR]- No other change. Once it is running this is the same skin as 0.1.22.[CR]- 0.1.22 was built but never published, and its zip asks for both add-ons. Use this one.[CR][CR][B]0.1.22[/B][CR]- Menu editor: the "Change action" row now reads "Movies / Titles" instead of "videodb://movies/titles/". Estuary 7 shows a readable name there; this closes that gap. Add-on paths show the add-on's own name.[CR]- Widgets: browsing into a widget no longer asks "Select Widget Type" when the answer is already known. It is taken from the type the widget declares, or worked out from the path you browsed to, so picking a movies list gives a movies widget without a second question.[CR]- That prompt was also the loop. Cancelling it threw the whole selection away and put you back at the start of the picker, which is why choosing a widget could feel like it never took.[CR]- Widgets: a plugin add-on picked from the add-ons list no longer gets stamped with the type "video", which is not a widget type at all and matched none of the skin's own conditions.[CR]- Needs script.estuary8.shortcuts 1.1.0 or newer. Install that zip first.[CR][CR][B]0.1.21[/B][CR]- Menu editor: "Change action" opens the shortcut picker. That is the whole point of this build. It used to open a raw keyboard prefilled with a string like ActivateWindow(Videos,videodb://movies/titles/,return), which is not something anyone should have to type.[CR]- NEITHER BUTTON WAS RENAMED. "Change action" is on the same button it was on, "Choose item for menu" is on the other, and both still match Estuary 7 one for one. Only the behaviour changed. Typing an action by hand is still there, on the item context menu as "Edit Action".[CR]- This needed a new add-on, script.estuary8.shortcuts, and it is ours: a fork of Skin Shortcuts 3.0.1 by MikeSiLVO, under its own add-on id, with his licence and credit unchanged.
